The copy floor is 60 tokens and 15 lines. Measured counts over the code formats of src and scripts with jscpd 5.4.2, the ladder that this floor came from: 495 clones at 60 tokens with 5 lines, 214 at 60/10, 48 at 60/15, 44 at 70/15, 0 at 100/20. Each report at 60/15 names a real repeated block; below it the set holds parameter tables, type declarations, and intra-file test noise whose repetition carries no name. A floor hides whole families, not only noise: the slug loop of src/lib/slug.ts existed in six production files, and the detector reported one pair of them, because a one-character difference drops each other pair below the floor. Thus the reason carries the ladder, so a future calibration re-runs the same measurement instead of a new judgment.

Ignored trees: node_modules and dist hold dependency and build output, not harness code. The gallery data directories data/, data.new/, and data.old/ hold generated gallery data; the hand-written gallery code beside them stays in the scan.

The data formats stay outside the scan: fixtures repeat data by design. A data gate would force destructured test payloads and give no gain.
